blocks.text: TWO MEN WHO "PROPHESIED IN THE CAMP" (NUMBERS 11:26) · EXODUS & WILDERNESS
Eldad and Medad. The spirit rested on them in the camp, and Moses would not forbid them.

HOW THE WORD CAME

THE CALL
How the word first came
NUMBERS 11 · THE SPIRIT IN THE CAMP
“and the spirit rested upon them; and they were of them that were written, but went not out unto the tabernacle: and they prophesied in the camp.”
Numbers 11:26 (KJV) →
HOW THE WORD KEPT COMING
"The spirit rested upon them", the same words used of the seventy at the tabernacle. Numbers 11:25–26
From the textNumbers says they "prophesied", but does not record anything they said. Numbers 11:26–27
BEFORE THE KINGS
Before Moses
LEADER OF ISRAEL, LAWGIVER AND PROPHET
Moses
“Enviest thou for my sake? would God that all the LORD’s people were prophets, and that the LORD would put his spirit upon them!”
Numbers 11:29 (KJV) →
PLACES
Where his story happened
The camp at Kibroth-hattaavah · The chapter’s camp is named in verse 34; the text does not name the place of the elders’ gathering separately.
COMPANIONS AND OPPONENTS
Who stood with him, and against him
Moses
Joshua
The seventy elders
HOW THE STORY ENDS
Scripture says, tradition says
SCRIPTURE SAYS
From the textScripture names them only in Numbers 11:26–27 and says nothing more of them. Numbers 11:26–27
TRADITION SAYS
No tradition is recorded here.
OPEN QUESTIONS
Where readers have differed
Yes, two of those chosen, who stayed in the camp
Keil (1871); Gray says this is how the verse "is generally understood"
Keil calls them "two of the persons who had been chosen", who "had remained behind in the camp, for some reason that is not reported".[4]
Of the wider body of elders, not of the seventy
Gray (1903)

Gray points out that verse 24 says the seventy went out to the tabernacle and verse 25 that the seventy received the spirit, and that Moses’ answer "implies that Eldad and Medad did not belong to the number". If the clause is original and not a later note, he says, it would be better to take "the registered" as "the whole body of elders from whom the seventy were chosen".[16]

WHAT SCRIPTURE DOES NOT SAY
Scripture does not give their tribe or family, why they stayed in the camp, or what they said.
Nothing is said of them after Numbers 11:27.
